heroHeadline: USCIS Requires Most Green Card Applicants to Leave the U.S. Under PM-602-0199 — 780,000+ Annual I-485 Filers Affected; Senate Still on Memorial Day Recess Without Voting on $71.7B ICE Package
heroSubtitle: On May 21–23, 2026, USCIS issued Policy Memorandum PM-602-0199, announcing that adjustment of status — the in-country green card application process used by roughly 780,000–800,000 applicants per year — will now be granted only in 'extraordinary circumstances.' The policy, covered by NPR, NBC News, CNN, and the Washington Post on May 22–23, requires most visa holders, immediate relatives of U.S. citizens, refugees, and work visa holders to leave the United States and apply through consulates abroad under the State Department's consular processing system. Immigration attorneys and advocacy organizations published urgent warnings for clients with pending I-485 applications, and the American Immigration Lawyers Association indicated it was reviewing PM-602-0199 for potential federal court challenge. The Senate remains on Memorial Day recess; the $71.7B ICE/CBP reconciliation package floor vote is now expected the week of June 1. ICE detention stands at a record 73,000+, the 287(g) local enforcement partnership program has reached 1,864 enrolled agencies (up 171% since January 2025), and Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons is set to depart May 31 when he will be succeeded by David Venturella — formerly of GEO Group.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, Congressional records, Roll Call, CBS News, NPR, NBC News, CNN, Washington Post, Boston Globe, Punchbowl News, Murthy Law Firm, and Vermont Public
